'''Mohamed Noor''' is the Executive Vice Provost<ref>Duke Today, [https://today.duke.edu/2024/06/mohamed-noor-appointed-executive-vice-provost "Mohamed Noor Appointed Executive Vice Provost"], retrieved 10 October 2024</ref> and a Professor in the Biology Department at [[Duke University]] (formerly holding the rotating titles of Earl D. McLean Professor,<ref>Duke Today, [https://today.duke.edu/2011/05/distprof11 "Duke Honors Distinguished Professors"], retrieved 21 July 2018</ref> department chair, dean of natural sciences,<ref>Duke Today, [https://today.duke.edu/2018/10/mohamed-noor-named-trinity-college-dean-natural-sciences "Mohamed Noor named Trinity College dean of natural sciences"], retrieved 21 August 2022</ref> Interim Dean of Arts & Sciences,<ref>Duke Today, [https://today.duke.edu/2022/04/mohamed-noor-named-interim-dean-trinity-college-arts-sciences "Mohamed Noor named Interim Dean of Trinity College of Arts & Sciences"], retrieved 21 August 2022</ref> and Interim Vice Provost for Academic Affairs<ref>Duke Today, [https://today.duke.edu/2022/12/noor-and-oates-serve-interim-vice-provost-roles "Noor and Oates to Serve in Interim Vice Provost Roles"], retrieved 1 February 2023</ref>). His specialties include [[evolution]], [[genetics]] and [[genomics]].

Noor has a BS from the [[College of William and Mary]] in 1992 and a PhD from [[University of Chicago]] (1996), together with a postdoctoral residency at [[Cornell University]] (1996&ndash;1998). He specializes in [[Drosophila]] evolution. His team's research approaches have included both classical genetic mapping, as well as analyses of whole genome sequences.<ref>Scudellari, Megan, [https://www.the-scientist.com/burgers-and-flies-41048 "Burgers and Flies"], ''The Scientist'', 1 May 2012, retrieved 21 July 2018</ref>

Likewise, Noor was one of the first scientists to demonstrate by experiment [[Reinforcement (speciation)|speciation by reinforcement]], that is, as a result of [[natural selection]] mating preferences diverge against deleterious [[Hybrid (biology)|hybridization]] and reduce gene flow between species. He is also known for developing (along with others) a model wherein regions of restricted recombination, as by [[chromosomal inversions]], facilitate the persistence of hybridizing species.<ref>Bates, Karl, [https://alumni.duke.edu/magazine/articles/descended-darwin "Descended from Darwin"], ''Duke Magazine'', 1 April 2009, retrieved 23 December 2019</ref>

Later, his research team has focused on understanding variation in recombination rate within and between species, and its impact on DNA sequence variation.

In 2008, he was awarded the [[Darwin-Wallace Medal]] from the Linnean Society of London.<ref>Duke Today, [https://today.duke.edu/2008/05/noor.html "Duke Biologist Wins Darwin-Wallace Medal"], retrieved 21 July 2018</ref>

In 2021, he was awarded a Friend of Darwin award by the [[National Center for Science Education]].<ref>{{cite web |last=Branch |first=Glenn |author-link=Glenn Branch |title=Friend of Darwin and Friend of the Planet awards for 2021 |url=https://ncse.ngo/friend-darwin-and-friend-planet-awards-2021 |website=National Center for Science Education |access-date=28 July 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210728183901/https://ncse.ngo/friend-darwin-and-friend-planet-awards-2021 |archive-date=28 July 2021}}</ref>

He served as editor-in-chief of the international journal ''[[Evolution (journal)|Evolution]]'' (2016-2019), is or was associate editor for several other journals, and the author of over 100 publications. He has served as president of the [[American Genetic Association]] (2012) and [[Society for the Study of Evolution]] (2014) and as a board member for the [[Genetics Society of America]].

Noor has been active in education and outreach, receiving numerous teaching and mentoring awards from his institution,<ref>Duke University Graduate School, [https://gradschool.duke.edu/about/news/2010-dean%E2%80%99s-award-mohamed-noor "2010 Dean's Award: Mohamed Noor"] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150713065800/https://gradschool.duke.edu/about/news/2010-dean%E2%80%99s-award-mohamed-noor |date=2015-07-13 }}, retrieved 21 July 2018</ref><ref>Duke Today, [https://today.duke.edu/2013/11/noor "Mohamed Noor: 'What Matters To Me and Why'"], retrieved 21 July 2018</ref> and teaching an online course in genetics and evolution. He and his group have also developed laboratory activities for implementation in high schools and colleges, including a commercial kit for observing natural selection in Drosophila. He published a book that uses [[Star Trek]] to teach principles in genetics and evolution,<ref>Noor, M. A. F. 2018. Live Long and Evolve: What Star Trek Can Teach Us about Evolution, Genetics, and Life on Other Worlds. Princeton University Press, Princeton, New Jersey. {{ISBN|978-0691177410}}, 208 pages.</ref> and gives classes and talks at various venues using science fiction to teach science.<ref>StarTrek.COM, [https://www.startrek.com/news/meet-college-professor-teaching-trek-millennials "Meet the College Professor Teaching 'Trek' to Millennials"], retrieved 23 December 2019</ref> On the side, he also serves as a science consultant for the [[Star Trek]] television franchise.<ref>IMDb listing, [https://www.imdb.com/name/nm11620507/], retrieved 17 October 2020</ref>

#Samuk, K., B. Manzano-Winkler, K. R. Ritz, and M. A. F. Noor. 2020. Natural selection shapes variation in genome-wide recombination rate in Drosophila pseudoobscura. Current Biology, 30: 1517-1528. [http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.cub.2020.03.053 abs].
